title: Build a bounded agent loop and check each trace
problem: An agent loop without an explicit budget and termination condition runs until something external stops it, and a checker that only reads final answers cannot see a forbidden attempt that was denied and retried. Both have to be designed, not assumed.
context: Builds on the trace format. The policy that chooses the next tool is a pluggable deterministic function; scripted policies stand in for a model. Tools are simulated functions over in-memory state.
impact: This is where the agent is bounded and its behavior first judged. Everything after it depends on traces being complete and checks being honest.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tools are registered explicitly with names and argument checks. A request for an unregistered tool is recorded as such and never executed.
The loop enforces a step budget and a termination condition, and records which ended the run. A policy that never finishes is stopped at the budget with a complete trace.
A declared set of forbidden tools is denied at call time, and every attempt is recorded in the trace even when denied.
Each trace is evaluated for task success against the scenario's expected end state, budget exhaustion, and forbidden attempts. A scenario that succeeds after a denied forbidden attempt reports both.
Automated tests cover a successful scenario, a non-terminating policy, an unknown tool, and a success after a denied forbidden attempt, and pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains the termination design, one rejected alternative (for example a wall-clock timeout), and what breaks first if a tool has a side effect the loop cannot observe.

constraints: Standard library plus a test runner only. No agent framework.
No network access and no model API. Every input is synthetic and generated or checked in by the learner.
Tools simulate effects in memory. Nothing touches the filesystem, network or shell.
Do not push to a remote or open a pull request as part of this task.

scope.description: A bounded loop that emits traces and a checker over them.

investigation_areas: What must be true for a loop to be guaranteed to stop
Where a forbidden action should be blocked, and why blocking alone is not enough
How task success is defined from end state rather than from the final message
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design; the learner chooses the runner and the layout.
documentation_requirements: Record the loop design, the check definitions and the rejected alternative in the learner design.
